name: Skyliner380
reference: proportions of the Airbus A380-800 (generic model, no branding; developer documentation only - do not use this wording in game UI)

axes.roblox_model_space: X = right/starboard, Y = up, -Z = forward (nose); right-handed
axes.blender: X = port(left), Y = aft, Z = up (nose points to -Y)
axes.hinge_axes: unit vectors in Roblox model space; positive angle = right-hand rule about the axis

joints: Every movable object has "parent" (the part it is jointed to), pivot, hinge_axis_roblox and rotation_limits_deg. A child rotation is applied relative to its parent (Motor6D chain): wheels -> bogie -> leg -> Fuselage for the body gears, wheels -> leg -> Fuselage otherwise. Retracted pose = every object at its "retracted_deg" (legs +, body-gear bogies -90).
origin: model origin = ground level (Y=0 at tyre contact), on the centreline, 35.50 m (126.79 studs) aft of the nose = centroid of the 20 main-gear wheels; this is the Model pivot when importing with "Set Pivot to Scene Origin"

mesh_notes.text: Every object is closed (0 non-manifold edges) with outward normals. Fuselage is one shell: the belly fairing is boolean-unioned into the tube. Objects listed in closed_shells_per_object are built from several closed shells that may intersect each other inside the object (e.g. wing + flap-track fairings, nacelle + core + pylon, gear cylinders, window panes, letters).

fbx.note: 1 Blender unit = 1 stud; raw FBX vertex numbers are studs

gltf.use: alternative for Roblox (Importer lists .gltf with multiple meshes, hierarchy, vertex colours); not tested in Studio
gltf.units: 1 glTF unit = 1 stud (Importer Scale Unit = Studs)
gltf.axes: raw glTF coordinates = FBX layout: X right, Y up, nose at -Z (scene turned 180 deg about the vertical before export). If Studio shows the nose at +Z, set World Forward = Back.

obj.use: DCC interchange only - NOT for Roblox
obj.note: OBJ stores no object transforms (every hinge/axle pivot is lost) and no vertex colours here (one Kd colour per object). The Roblox Importer lists multiple meshes / hierarchies / vertex colours only for .fbx and .gltf; merged, the OBJ would exceed 20,000 triangles.

roblox_import.after_import: set every MeshPart.Color = (255,255,255): Roblox multiplies vertex colours with MeshPart.Color (default Medium Stone Grey)

motion_checks.method: generalised winding number (inside >= 0.5) of posed vertices against closed target meshes; poses = manifest pivots, hinge axes and rotation limits (children follow their "parent" chain)
